- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply linear decay bias: reduce forecast by 0.1–0.3% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid “bear trap” bias.
